issues.legal_issue: Land classified as communal tank poramboke and vested in the government is unavailable for grant of a ryotwari patta.
material_facts: The entire survey area was classified as Peddacheruvu Tank Poramboke in a District Gazette notification and treated as communal land.
The claimants sought implementation of purported ryotwari pattas for plots within that survey area.
The Gazette notification classifying the land was not challenged by the claimants.
issues.conclusion: The land vested in the government free from encumbrances and no ryotwari patta could be granted or implemented for it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2-A of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Area) Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1956 transfers communal lands, porambokes, tanks and tank beds in inam lands to the government free from encumbrances. Section 7 permits grant of ryotwari pattas only in accordance with the Act; land vested under Section 2-A is not available for such a grant.

predicates.appeal_from_refusal_to_implement_ryotwar: The claimant appealed after an authority refused to implement a purported ryotwari patta.
predicates.land_classified_as_communal_tank: The relevant land was officially classified as communal tank or tank-poramboke land.
predicates.classification_notification_not_challeng: The claimant did not challenge the official notification that classified the land.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns refusal to implement a patta for land officially classified as communal tank land and that classification is unchallenged, the land is unavailable for a ryotwari patta.

issues.legal_issue: A court exercising judicial review does not interfere with an administrative decision supported by record material absent a reviewable defect, or re-decide disputed factual questions as an appellate court.
material_facts: The Collector conducted an enquiry pursuant to a court direction and relied on materials including the absence of the purported pattas from official records and the official tank classification.
The claimants disputed the genuineness and validity of the pattas and the character of the land.
The High Court declined to reanalyse the evidence or determine those disputed facts, and the Supreme Court found no patent illegality or irrationality warranting interference.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right not to interfere with the Collector's decision in judicial review.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226 of the Constitution, administrative decisions may be reviewed for grounds including perversity, patent illegality, irrationality, want of power and procedural irregularity. Judicial review is directed to the decision-making process, not an appeal on the merits; courts do not reanalyse evidence or adjudicate hotly disputed facts in that jurisdiction.

rule.if: article_226_review_of_administrative_decision and decision_based_on_record_materials and disputed_facts_require_reassessment and not patent_reviewable_defect

predicates.article_226_review_of_administrative_dec: A party sought judicial review of an administrative decision.
predicates.decision_based_on_record_materials: The decision-maker relied on materials in the record when reaching the decision.
predicates.disputed_facts_require_reassessment: Resolving the challenge would require the court to reanalyse evidence or decide disputed facts.
predicates.patent_reviewable_defect: The decision contains a patent illegality, perversity, irrationality, want of power or procedural irregularity warranting review.

issues.definition: Where judicial review is sought against a record-based administrative decision, and resolving the challenge requires reassessing disputed facts without a patent reviewable defect, the decision is not disturbed.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant cannot obtain relief against a decision resting on an official land-classification notification while leaving that notification unchallenged.
material_facts: The Collector relied on a Gazette notification classifying the entire survey area as tank poramboke when refusing implementation of the purported pattas.
The claimants challenged the Collector's refusal but did not challenge the Gazette notification itself.
issues.conclusion: The claimants could not obtain an order quashing the Collector's decision without challenging the notification on which it rested.
issues.legal_principle: Where the challenged administrative decision rests on an operative land-classification notification, a party seeking relief that depends on undoing that classification must challenge the notification; the Court relied on the claimants' omission to do so.

predicates.writ_challenging_decision_based_on_land_: A claimant sought judicial relief against a decision that relied on an official land-classification notification.
predicates.claimant_did_not_challenge_underlying_no: The claimant did not challenge the notification that supplied the basis for the decision.

issues.definition: A claimant challenging a decision based on an official land notification, but not the notification itself, does not obtain relief that depends on setting that decision aside.

issues.legal_issue: Relief under Article 226 may be refused when a claimant delays asserting a claimed right beyond a reasonable time.
material_facts: The governing enactment had been in force for many years before the claimant applied for a ryotwari patta.
The claimant sought relief in writ proceedings after that prolonged delay.
issues.conclusion: Relief was also liable to be refused for delay, laches, acquiescence or omission to assert the claimed right within a reasonable time.
issues.legal_principle: The extraordinary remedy under Article 226 may be refused where delay, laches, acquiescence or failure to assert a right within a reasonable time makes relief inappropriate. The Court also noted that the governing enactment contemplated an application soon after its commencement.

predicates.article_226_claim_for_ryotwari_patta: A claimant sought a ryotwari patta through writ proceedings.
predicates.claimant_delayed_asserting_right_beyond_: The claimant waited beyond a reasonable time after the relevant opportunity arose before asserting the claimed right.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks a ryotwari patta through writ proceedings but delays asserting the claim beyond a reasonable time, writ relief may be refused for delay.

issues.legal_issue: Water bodies and their beds are inalienable and cannot be granted to an individual even if they are dry or disused.
material_facts: The survey area was officially declared to be a tank, although the claimants asserted rights over plots within it and cultivation had been claimed.
The Court noted that cultivation may occur on a dried water-body bed without changing its character as a water body.
issues.conclusion: No patta or transfer could be granted over the land as a water body, including if it had dried up or fallen into disuse.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Section 2-A of the 1956 Act and held that water bodies are inalienable, including when dry or disused. It cited Susetha v. State of Tamil Nadu, (2006) 6 SCC 543; M.C. Mehta (Badkhal and Surajkund Lakes Matter) v. Union of India, (1997) 3 SCC 715; and Intellectuals Forum v. State of Andhra Pradesh, (2006) 3 SCC 549.

predicates.claim_for_pattta_or_transfer: A claimant sought a patta or transfer of the relevant land.
predicates.land_is_water_body: The land is a water body or its bed, whether or not it is currently dry or in use.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks a patta or transfer of land that is a water body or its bed, the land is not alienable.
